title: Post-Selection Coverage of Wald Intervals after Choosing Proxy Roles in Proximal Synthetic Control
banked_reason: D0.5.G: meets_floor=false, tier=incremental, paper_score_ceiling=6.4<7.4, salvageable=false; the corrected uniform result requires oracle stabilization and the advertised West-German rectangular rule remains outside the theorem.
gap_reasons: The corrected uniform result holds only after imposing common finite-row oracle-variance and horizon bounds, and the note supplies no observable procedure for verifying those oracle bounds in the intended application.

The West-German redesign is not executed and the actual rectangular simplex-constrained rule is outside the theorem, leaving the practical significance supported only by a narrow two-role square-bridge construction and its synthetic witnesses.
The note is mathematically repairable, but another D0 return would only repair correctness and disclosure; it would not cure the round-2 field-tier judgment.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the selected-Gaussian coverage algebra, exact tie protection, an asymmetric primitive Gaussian undercoverage witness, and a maximal broad-class uniform-failure construction. The proposed positive uniform correction survived only on a class with oracle finite-row stabilization, while the six-coordinate joint CLT and exact Shi-class transfer remained undischarged. Reaching field tier would require observable stabilization theory or a genuine rectangular West-German application, not another bounded correctness pass.
tldr: Two predeclared valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet yield a nonregular conventional interval when the smaller full-pre-period ridge loss selects the reported role. The exact selected-Gaussian coverage map protects every symmetric Wald level at an exact tie and protects every local gap exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared selector correlations; otherwise the strict coverage-error sign is the gap sign times their squared-correlation difference. A constant-treatment one-factor Gaussian chart realizes both regimes inside a stationary square subclass of the Shi et al. model, including an open asymmetric region with coverage \(0.8857757910650707\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval. For correction, an early selector, logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fit, post average, and future-only Bartlett standard error are uniformly selector-conditionally normal on the strengthened class with common finite-row horizon and scalar variance bounds. The same claim fails maximally on the broader pointwise-limit class, where expected conditional Kolmogorov distance can converge to one.
gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and proxy roles, while general selective-inference theory does not characterize unconditional conventional symmetric-Wald coverage for a statistic that changes coordinates with the selected role.
fill: The paper supplies the selected limit, the evaluable coverage map, the squared-correlation frontier and strict sign rule, a continuous finite-dimensional primitive realization map, and a separated estimator whose uniform singular-covariance mapping over bounded-gap triangular arrays is exposed as the first-class open question.
